title: Y9T End-of-Line Test Station
short: Every Y9T unit needed a fast, consistent final check — with recorded results for each part.
problem: Final verification of every Y9T unit had to be consistent, fast and fully traceable, with clear pass/fail records.
solution: A turnkey station at the final verification zone. When a part is clamped, the software handshakes with the PLC, runs 14 parametric, resistance and sensor checks in parallel, applies a pass/fail matrix with auto-retest tolerance, prints a serialised QA label and logs every result against the production serial number.
features: High-speed handshake with the line PLC to read sensor inputs on part clamp
Multithreaded WPF test sequencer running 14 parametric checks in parallel
Pass/fail decision matrix with auto-retest tolerance to avoid false rejects
Automatic serialised QA label printing and pneumatic pass/reject diversion
software: SQL Server with local SQLite buffer

title: YG8 End-of-Line Quality & Safety Station
short: Operators needed a fast inspection station that that checks station readiness before inspection.
problem: The YG8 line needed a quick operator inspection station that could show interlock status before inspection, and that stayed readable on a high-glare shop floor.
solution: A dedicated inspection station with dual-channel safety light curtains, pneumatic locks and a high-contrast touchscreen WPF interface. Seating-pressure curves are plotted live against threshold envelopes, and results are committed to SQL only after the physical interlock releases.
features: Safety light-curtain state read directly from PLC memory bits
Touchscreen UI designed for high-glare shop-floor readability
Live seating-pressure curves with threshold envelopes
Database transaction committed only after the interlock releases

title: Production Progress SMS Alerts
short: Supervisors and maintenance learned about stoppages and missed targets too late — often only at shift end.
problem: Shift supervisors and maintenance teams found out about line stoppages and missed hourly targets too late to act on them.
solution: A Windows service that monitors line registers and databases, compares hourly progress with the schedule and sends SMS summaries through an industrial GSM modem to a tiered roster of managers, engineers and maintenance — with immediate alarms when downtime exceeds a threshold.
features: Background service polling line databases and PLC state words
RS-232 AT-command handler with automatic baud negotiation and retry
Tiered recipient roster for managers, engineers and maintenance
Immediate alarm when downtime exceeds a set limit (e.g. 5 minutes)

title: Automated Shift Production Reports
short: Daily output, scrap and OEE were logged by hand on paper, taking time and inviting errors.
problem: Line output, scrap and downtime were recorded manually on paper every shift — slow, error-prone and hard to analyse.
solution: A scheduled reporting service that runs at the end of each shift, aggregates production, scrap, downtime and station pace from SQL, calculates OEE, and emails multi-tab Excel workbooks and PDF summaries with charts — over authenticated SMTP with a backup relay.
features: Scheduler triggered at the end of each shift rotation
SQL aggregation of output vs scrap, downtime and station pace
Headless PDF summaries with embedded charts plus multi-tab Excel
TLS-authenticated SMTP with backup relay failover

title: Magnatest-D Eddy-Current Sorting & Reporting
short: Heat-treated fasteners needed individual hardness checks — sampling left gaps in inspection coverage.
problem: Heat-treated automotive fasteners needed every part verified for hardness and permeability deviations; manual sampling left gaps.
solution: An acquisition and sorting interface for FOERSTER Magnatest-D eddy-current instruments. It streams impedance vectors over RS-232, matches them against calibrated master-part tolerance curves, and fires pneumatic gates to route each part to OK, Re-treat or Scrap — with batch histograms for metallurgical tracking.
features: Real-time RS-232 acquisition of impedance vectors (X, Y)
Elliptical tolerance matching against calibrated master parts
Pneumatic gate routing into OK, Re-treat or Scrap bins
Shift distribution histograms and batch tracking

title: Andon Shop-Floor Visual Management
short: Bottlenecks, stoppages and maintenance calls weren’t visible to everyone on the floor in real time.
problem: Line status, bottlenecks and maintenance calls were not visible to the whole floor as they happened, slowing the response.
solution: Overhead 65-inch line displays showing live throughput, takt-time progress, Andon cord pulls and maintenance response timers — driven by a SignalR hub with colour-coded status and audible alarms for critical faults.
features: Distributed clients updated over SignalR / WebSockets
Colour-coded status: green normal, yellow warning, red stoppage
Audible alarm for critical faults
Takt-time progress synchronised with the assembly conveyor
hardware: Raspberry Pi / Intel NUC client nodes
software: C# WPF full-screen client / web dashboard

title: Finished-Goods Scan & Dispatch Confirmation
short: Mismatched variants being packed together caused shipping errors and customer returns.
problem: Mismatched part variants occasionally ended up in the same shipment, leading to packing errors and customer return claims.
solution: A finished-goods checkpoint where a fixed-mount imager reads 2D DataMatrix/QR codes automatically, parses part number, lot and date, and confirms them against open SAP production orders. A pneumatic gate lock stops mismatched parts from entering the crate, and a local SQLite store keeps the station running if the network drops.
features: Fixed-mount imager triggered automatically by a proximity sensor
Parser for part numbers, supplier lot IDs and manufacturing dates
Quantity confirmation against the order before the box is sealed
Pneumatic gate lock blocks mismatched items from the crate

title: High-Speed Conveyor RFID Encoding
short: Each pallet needed unique genealogy data written to its RFID tag — without slowing or stopping the conveyor.
problem: Every pallet needed its component genealogy written to an RFID tag on the move, without stopping or slowing the conveyor.
solution: An inline UHF RFID cell that uses rotary-encoder position to trigger the antenna, writes 96-bit EPC data to moving pallet tags, verifies each write by reading it back, and ejects pallets whose tags fail or respond with a weak signal.
features: Rotary encoder pulses locate the pallet and trigger the antenna
LLRP commands write 96-bit EPC memory without stopping the line
Read-after-write verification before the pallet leaves the antenna field
Automatic rejection when a write fails or RSSI is too low

title: Machine Vision Defect Inspection
short: Manual visual checks for burrs, scratches and missing O-rings were subjective and time-consuming.
problem: Manual inspection for micro-burrs, scratches and missing O-rings was subjective, tiring and consumed many inspector hours.
solution: An optical QC station with diffused and coaxial lighting and a 5 MP industrial camera, triggered by the PLC when the jig is seated. It measures diameters with sub-pixel edge detection, overlays defects on the operator screen and blows off rejects automatically.
features: Hardware trigger from the PLC when the jig is seated
Sub-pixel edge detection for inner/outer diameters against configured tolerances
Live defect overlay on the operator monitor
Automatic OK / defect sorting with pneumatic blow-off

title: Gearbox Dynamic Test Bench
short: Every gearbox needed a documented endurance and efficiency test, with safe shutdown if limits were exceeded.
problem: Each gearbox needed a documented endurance and efficiency test, with protection against overheating or over-torque during the run.
solution: An automated bench that ramps drive speed through a VFD, samples torque, RPM and bearing temperature over Modbus RTU, plots torque-vs-RPM curves live, and trips a safe shutdown with brake lock if thermal or torque limits are breached — then issues a PDF test certificate.
features: Continuous Modbus RTU polling of torque transducers and encoders
Automated motor speed ramp via VFD serial commands
Real-time torque-vs-RPM curves
Automatic shutdown and brake lock on thermal or torque trip
